messages.text:
Dear Support Team,

I am writing to report an issue I am experiencing with my Thor P2
<http://192.168.68.101/> miner. Currently, the device is only producing *4.8
TH/s*, and diagnostics indicate that only one chip is carrying the hashrate
instead of operating at full cap····.

Here are the current operational details from the web interface:

   -

   *Hashrate:* 4.8 TH/s (out of expected performance)
   -

   *Power Draw:* 155.0 W (Estimated wall power max 240 W)
   -

   *ASIC Temperature:* 46.3 °C
   -

   *VR Temperature:* 73.0 °C
   -

   *Connected Pools:* solo.atlaspool.io <http://192.168.68.101/> (Pool 1)
   and parasite.wtf <http://192.168.68.101/> (Pool 2)

Could you please advise on troubleshooting steps to check or reinitialize
the inactive chips and restore full hashrate performance?

Best regards,

Clovil J.
Searched the web · Hammer Thor P2 miner 10TH ASIC chip count BM1370
Handed to the team · Needs JD's official Thor P2 Thor OS image and his call on single-chip enumeratio

Hi Clovil,

Thanks for the detailed numbers, they actually tell us a lot.

The T. P2 is a dual chip board, two Bitmain BM1373s, rated around 10 TH/s for roughly 155 to 166 W at the wall. What you are seeing is 4.8 TH/s for 155 W, which works out at about 32 J/TH, almost exactly double the efficiency the unit is specified at. That is the useful clue: if one chip had genuinely died, the wall draw would fall to somewhere near 80 W. It has not. The board is still feeding and powering both chips, and only one of them is being enumerated and given work. That is a firmware and chip detection problem, not a cooked board, and it fits the timing, since this started after the move from Thor OS to Harlo OS. Your 46.3 C chip temperature confirms nothing is thermally throttling, and 73 C on the VR is warm but within normal for this board under load.

Chip enumeration only happens at a cold boot, so start there. Unplug the miner at the wall, leave it off for a full minute, then power it back up, and do not use the reboot button in the UI, as that does not always re-scan the chain. When it comes back, look at the main page for the ASIC or chip count. If it reads 1 instead of 2, the firmware is only finding half the board, and that is the whole story behind the 4.8 TH/s.

If it still reads one chip, two things to do in order. First, check in the Harlo OS settings that the device model or board profile selected is the Thor P2 dual BM1373 one and not a single chip profile, since the wrong profile will drive only the first chip. Second, go to the Firmware updates section in the Harlo OS UI and apply the latest OTA image, which keeps your settings. Compare what the unit reports against the current release listed on https://harlolabs.com/ and update if you are behind. If it is on the latest already, do a factory reset from the UI and set your pool back up fresh, because a settings file carried over from an earlier version is a common cause of a half detected chain.

Your pool side is fine and is not involved in this, so leave it alone. solo.atlaspool.io on Stratum V1 with parasite.wtf as the backup is a correct setup, and a pool will always report a lower, slower moving number than the unit's own display.

On going back to Thor OS, I do not want you flashing an image off a forum, as the P2 chain is picky and a bad flash is hard to undo. JD, our hardware lead, has the official file and I have passed him your full picture, including the single chip detection under Harlo OS. A colleague is picking this up today and you will get the file and his read back in this thread. If you want the fastest route in the meantime, our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf is where JD lives, mention @nullhashrate and he will answer you there directly.

Send me the chip count after the cold boot and the Harlo OS version it reports, and I will take it from there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
